clue.text: Tons in store, say, for competitor in field event

indicators.note: one item sitting in another means it is placed inside that word

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for tons
to say something is to utter it

explanation.surface: Someone stockpiling tons in a shop, apparently to equip an athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field event' sounds like the definition's end, but the whole phrase from 'competitor' is the definition; 'say' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: The shot put is a throwing event held in the field part of athletics, so its athlete is a competitor there.

clue.text: Cut off, erring in appeal for help not sharply defined

indicators.note: letters that err stray from their proper places, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: SOS is the distress signal asking for help

explanation.surface: Someone cut off by mistake while making a call for help.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CUT OFF are mixed with SOS to give SOFT-FOCUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft focus is a photographic effect where images are deliberately blurred, with edges left fuzzy and imprecise.

clue.text: Smell food, so hurry, deprived of regular portions

indicators.note: losing portions at regular intervals means every other letter goes, leaving the rest

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters are kept

explanation.surface: A hurried meal where everyone gets only meagre helpings.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a smell, the two words being straightforward synonyms for a scent noticed by the nose.

clue.text: Upright fellow with second innings in game

indicators.note: with means these parts are joined one after another in order

blocks.note: a post is an upright pole
S is the abbreviation for second
in cricket a batsman's innings is called a knock

explanation.surface: An upright sort taking his second turn at the crease in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: POST + MAN + S + KNOCK. 'Innings' and 'game' suggest cricket, but the answer is a party game.
explanation.definitionFit: Postman's knock is a traditional children's party game in which players exchange kisses for imaginary letters.

clue.text: Metal casing that is forming connection

indicators.note: a casing wraps around something, so the metal surrounds the other part

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A metal case making a link between parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' is the English reading of the Latin abbreviation i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is a link or association between two things, such as a product connected to a film.

clue.text: Outgoing traveller, on time after departure, missing one

indicators.note: something missing is lost, so a letter is dropped from that word
one piece placed after another sets out the order of the parts

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A traveller arriving punctually after leaving, though one person has gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing one' applies only to the departure word, not the traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: Outgoing describes a sociable personality, and an extrovert is someone with exactly that friendly, confident temperament.

clue.text: Unwanted messages in charts going around

indicators.note: going around turns the word to face the other way, so it is read backwards

explanation.surface: Junk mail being passed round among a set of charts.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is the familiar name for unsolicited email, especially bulk advertising sent to many inboxes at once.

clue.text: Maintains power over substitutes

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means the first piece sits above the second

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A coach keeping control over the players on the bench.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to keep it in its existing condition, which is what maintaining it means.

clue.text: Without source of light I'm upset

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset turns the words upside down, reading them from the bottom

blocks.note: the sun is our source of daylight

explanation.surface: Someone distressed at being left without a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Minus can be used as a preposition for lacking something, as in 'minus his coat', matching without.

clue.text: Storm, test for men at sea throughout

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A storm testing sailors through their whole voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: The nautical answer fits the sea picture neatly; 'at sea' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: From stem to stern means from the front of a ship to its back, hence completely or all over.

clue.text: Extra flexible with translation of any term

indicators.note: translating changes the form of words, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A translator allowing some leeway in rendering any word.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplementary describes something added on to complete or enlarge a thing, so it means additional or extra.

clue.text: Supervisor in favour of returning call

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for call is read backwards

blocks.note: to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: A manager keen for someone to call back.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreman is a worker who directs and oversees a team, as on a building site or factory floor.

clue.text: Burden quietly accepted by old journalists

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so it goes inside the other words

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A quiet hardship borne by veteran reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: P is taken in by O + PRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to weigh down heavily on people, as a verb meaning to burden or load with hardship.

clue.text: Chapter, part containing good unfinished record of events

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so the final letter is dropped
containing means holding something within, so the next word goes inside

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for chapter
a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: A chapter of a book that tells only part of a good story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like it belongs with 'Chapter' as a section of a book, but it means a role in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a factual written account of happenings arranged in the order they took place.

clue.text: Group filled with energy when working and thinking

indicators.note: something filled with other things holds them inside it

blocks.note: a ring is a group, such as a gang
E is the symbol for energy
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A lively team, busy at work and full of ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' and 'working' each give a short word, a common crossword economy.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning is the mental process of working things out logically, so it is a form of thinking.

clue.text: Finish with king and fool bound together

indicators.note: with means the following pieces are added on in sequence

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch and his jester ending up tied to each other.
explanation.walkthrough: A nit (short for nitwit) is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-knit group is tightly united, its members closely bound to one another by shared bonds.

clue.text: Raging against one breaking cover

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so these letters go within

blocks.note: v is short for versus, against
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Fury at someone blowing another's undercover identity.
explanation.definitionFit: Livid is an informal way of saying furiously angry, the state of someone who is raging.

clue.text: Wanted around Panama, lost hope

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first word wraps the second

blocks.note: PA is the abbreviation for Panama

explanation.surface: A fugitive in Panama giving up on escape.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to give up all expectation of things improving, the past tense matching lost hope.

clue.text: Careless in head of state's absence

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter only

explanation.surface: A negligent official, sloppy while the president is away.
explanation.definitionFit: Slack describes someone lax or negligent in their work, not taking due care over it.

clue.text: Cheerful people I spot, excited about film

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so they move into a new order
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the film

blocks.note: a mist is a thin film of moisture

explanation.surface: A happy movie fan spotting something thrilling about a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests a movie, but here it is a thin layer, MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimists are people who expect the best outcome, so they are naturally hopeful and cheerful.

clue.text: Anger acceptable in show

indicators.note: one thing placed in another goes inside that word

explanation.surface: Fury being treated as fine in a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To provoke someone is to deliberately stir up their irritation, so it is a verb meaning to anger them.

clue.text: Difficult question for exhibitionist

blocks.note: second meaning: someone who strikes attitudes to be admired

explanation.surface: Putting a tricky question to a show-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is both a baffling problem to solve and a person who poses affectedly to impress others.

clue.text: Musical piece from applicant at audition

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A performer singing a piece at an audition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a medium-length vocal composition with instrumental accompaniment, often with solos and chorus.

clue.text: Cloak right for illicit activity

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: The proper cloak for a cloak-and-dagger job.
explanation.definitionFit: Caper is informal for a criminal escapade or heist, a piece of illicit activity.

clue.text: Restless, say, bothered about part of Bible

indicators.note: bothered means troubled and stirred up, so these letters are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the other part

explanation.surface: Someone fidgety and troubled over a passage of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Antsy is informal for agitated or fidgety, unable to keep still, like having ants in your pants.

clue.text: Criticism popular doctor alters, changing dressing

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the letters of the word next to it are reordered

blocks.note: stick is informal for harsh criticism
a GP is a general practitioner

explanation.surface: A well-liked doctor criticised for altering a wound's covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like an anagram signal but gives GP; 'changing' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticking plaster is the British term for an adhesive bandage, a small dressing for cuts.

clue.text: Outfit beginning to accumulate capital

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter alone

blocks.note: a rig is an outfit of clothing or equipment

explanation.surface: Kit for someone starting to build up savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money, matching accumulate, but it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga is the capital city of Latvia, on the Baltic coast.

clue.text: Like an idealist, waited to receive right cereal

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in, so these go inside

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A dreamer hanging on for the correct breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cereal' suggests breakfast food, but it means a grain crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Starry-eyed means naively romantic or unrealistically hopeful, the outlook of a dreamy idealist.
